commits.title: A seeded 48-product category holds a full listing at 20 router requests

changes.how: Add export async function fullCategory(storeId: string, count = 48): Promise<{ slug: string }>. It makes `count` active products in the store as copies of the demo tote bag and puts them in a new category. Port the helper manyProducts() of src/server/listing.int.test.ts (lines 150 to 190: read it first; it copies the product with handle 'demo-handlenett', its translations, variants, prices through commerce.set_price and media) from drizzle's sql to this file's postgres.js client (testDb()): use sql.begin(async (tx) => { ... }) for the transaction, tx.unsafe(text) for the statements that splice the column lists, and the same temp tables. Use the handles 'full-1' to 'full-48' and titles 'Full 01' to 'Full 48'. Then insert the category as e2e/signed-in/collections.spec.ts lines 40 to 44 do: insert into commerce.terms (store_id, content_type, kind, name, slug) values (storeId, 'product', 'category', 'Full kategori', 'full') returning id, and one row of commerce.product_terms (store_id, product_id, term_id) per copied product. Return { slug: 'full' }. Close the client in a finally, as the file's other helpers do.

Step 0.14 made this file (or added to step 0.12's): its helper routerPrefetches(page), called BEFORE page.goto, returns an array that fills with { url, segment } for every request carrying both the rsc and next-router-prefetch headers. Step 1.3 added the table ROUTER_REQUESTS: Record<string, number> keyed by fixed addresses of the demo store, with one phone test per row and a scroll-to-the-footer function; step 2.6 set its rows and added 'a footer link waits to be pointed at'. Do not add a row to ROUTER_REQUESTS (this store's slug is made per run, so it cannot be a fixed key): beside the table write `const FULL_LISTING_MOST = 20; // a 48-product category read to the end on a phone (bloat review step 2.8)` and use it in the new test. Add a test 'a full listing read to the end fetches no more than 20 pages ahead': const store = await testStore('prefetch-full'); const { slug } = await fullCategory(store.id); a phone page (viewport 390 by 844, isMobile and hasTouch, as 1.3's phone tests set them); const seen = routerPrefetches(page) before page.goto(`/s/${store.slug}/no/category/${slug}`) (the long address with the market, as e2e/terms.spec.ts line 55 writes one); expect page.locator("main a[href*='/p/full-']") to have count 48; wait 3 s; then scroll to the end in steps of one screen with 300 ms between (await page.mouse.wheel(0, 800) in a loop until window.scrollY stops growing; reuse 1.3's scroll function if it does exactly this), wait 3 s more; expect seen.length to be at most FULL_LISTING_MOST, with the message naming seen.map((r) => r.url). Second expectation: the set of different '/p/full-' handles among seen's urls has at most 6 members (the first screen). Third, in the same test: const before = seen.length; focus the 21st tile's link (await page.locator("main a[href*='/p/full-']").nth(20).focus(): PolicyLink asks on focus as on pointer enter and touch) and expect, within 2 s (expect.poll), seen to hold one more request whose url contains that tile's handle.

commits.title: The partial-prefetching trial on four pages, and the decision it led to

changes.how: The trial's raw output, so the table in docs/performance.md only copies numbers from it: a title '# The partial-prefetching trial (bloat review step 2.8)', the date, the commit the builds were made from and the Next version; then, per destination and per build (before, after), a fenced block with the exact lines the counter printed (the router request count and the addresses, or measure-routes.mjs's output for the bytes) and the three press-to-heading timings in ms with how each was read. Write nothing in it you did not see printed. Lines at most 130 characters except inside the fenced blocks.

This commit changes documents only; the trial itself is run locally and none of its code is pushed. The trial: for each of four destinations, one at a time and each in its own production build (pnpm build, pnpm start on the seeded database plus the 48-product category of commit 2), add the line export const prefetch = 'partial'; to the destination's page file, measure, and remove the line again (git checkout the file). The four: the product page src/app/s/[store]/[market]/p/[handle]/page.tsx; the category listing's page (the page.tsx under src/app/s/[store]/[market]/category that draws term-listing.tsx); the store home src/app/s/[store]/[market]/page.tsx; the admin's orders page src/app/admin/(gated)/[store]/orders/page.tsx (measured in the signed-in stand-in build, E2E_SIGNED_IN=1, with e2e/signed-in/prefetch.spec.ts). Measure for each, before (no line) and after (with it): (a) router prefetch requests and their decoded bytes on the page that links to the destination, read to the end on a phone: for the product page that linking page is the seeded category (/s/<store>/no/category/full), for the listing it is the store home, for the store home it is a product page (its logo and menu), for orders it is the admin home at 1280 px; use the counter of e2e/prefetch.spec.ts with the count printed, or node docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/measure-routes.mjs <outDir> for the bytes; (b) what is on screen at the press: press the link and note whether the destination's heading and price (or the orders table) are drawn at once or after a fetch (time from the press to the heading visible, three runs, the median). Add to the section '## What the router fetches ahead' (step 2.6 made it; create it if missing) a sub-heading 'The partial-prefetching trial (bloat review step 2.8)' with: the date, the Next version (rg '"next":' package.json), one table with a row per destination and the columns: linking page | requests before | requests after | bytes before | bytes after | ms to heading before | ms to heading after; each figure copied from docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/evidence/partial-prefetching-trial.md (the medians computed from its three timings), with a link to that file; then the decision in two or three sentences. Then add two rows to the policy table of that section: 'product tiles: the first six of a listing on sight, the rest on intent (SIGHT_TILES in src/components/product-card.tsx)' and 'swatches under a tile and category chips: intent'. Lines at most 130 characters; table rows at most 300.

In the rule about links that step 2.6 added ('## Links say what they may fetch ahead ...'; find it with rg -n 'fetch ahead' docs/rules/storefront.md) add one sentence: a listing draws its first six tiles with policy sight and the rest with intent (`SIGHT_TILES`, `ProductGrid`), swatches and chips with intent, and `e2e/prefetch.spec.ts` holds a 48-product category at 20 router requests.
